blocks.body:
## Executive Summary

- **The supplied trip spending totals $1,501.89.** This includes $1,351.66 on fully dated trip receipts, $75.23 on provisionally included undated receipts, and $75.00 you reported separately. The miscellaneous $25.00 is estimated. Two July receipts totaling $134.42 are excluded.
- **Fuel is the largest expense: $890.23, or 59.3% of the included total.** The 16 fully quantified fuel purchases account for 179.718 gallons at a gallon-weighted effective price of $4.675 per gallon; the additional $50.00 fuel allocation has no supplied volume or unit price and is excluded from that average. Food and drinks account for another $537.86.
- **Utah has the most recorded spending, at $506.03.** Among fully dated receipts, Aug 17, 2026 is the highest-spending day: $296.14 across 7 purchases. The undated and manual payments cannot be assigned to a day.

This total includes the user-confirmed v2 override alongside supplied receipts and additions; it is not a verified complete cost of the family trip. No lodging payments or mileage records were provided.

## V2 correction adds $50.00 to recorded spending

The August 17 Maverik purchase in Green River, Wyoming is recorded as **$53.37**, replacing $3.37, following your explicit confirmation. The original printed itemization still reconciles to $3.37 ($3.18 plus $0.19 tax); $53.37 is a **user-confirmed override**, not a newly verified printed amount.

You subsequently confirmed that the additional **$50.00 is fuel**. It is now included in fuel spending, with no unallocated balance. Its gallons, grade, and unit price remain unknown, so it is excluded from fuel-price averages. The known $3.37 convenience-drink allocation and printed tax are unchanged. This replaces one receipt total and does not add another payment.

## The spending total has a clear evidence boundary

**The trip window is Aug 14, 2026 through Aug 30, 2026, inclusive.** The included total covers 43 image-backed purchases and 2 manual additions. A receipt’s final charged total is counted once; card-payment sections, subtotals and individual line items are not added again.

The table separates payments with fully readable trip dates from the four undated receipts and your manual additions. Only fully dated receipts enter the daily chart. July purchases contribute nothing to the trip comparisons below; only their aggregate exclusion count and amount are public. All amounts are US dollars.

## Fuel accounts for 59.3% of supplied spending

**Fuel leads at $890.23; restaurants and prepared meals follow at $308.56.** Read the bars as all-in spending by what was purchased, rather than by the kind of store. Prepared Maverik meals count as restaurants; gas remains fuel; nonfood Walmart items keep their own categories.

Discounts reduce the related category. Receipt taxes are allocated across item categories where necessary, so mixed-receipt category totals are estimates at the category level even though they reconcile exactly to the charged receipt. Fuel tax is generally embedded in the pump price, not an additional amount. The checkout-bag fee is grouped with groceries, not shown as a separate spending category.

Fuel includes the $50.00 user-confirmed allocation. The previously captured $0.19 tax remains with its known convenience-drink item; no extra tax or tip is inferred for the fuel correction.
The exact category amounts below make small purchases visible even when their bars are too short to compare. Category transaction counts can overlap when one receipt contains more than one category.

## Restaurants cost about 1.9 times the grocery spending

**Food and drinks total $537.86, or 35.8% of included spending.** Restaurant and prepared-meal purchases total $308.56, including the $50 Utah steakhouse payment. Groceries total $163.72; convenience snacks and drinks add $65.58.

The grocery category includes food and drinks bought at grocery stores and Walmart; convenience snacks/drinks describes those purchases at travel stops and similar outlets. This distinction is useful for planning the next trip, but it does not establish when the food was eaten. No separate steakhouse tax, tip, menu items or purchase date were supplied, so the reported $50 is counted as one all-in payment. Grocery spending includes associated checkout-bag charges, grouped there at your request.

## Utah and Colorado account for 56.0% of spending

**Utah leads with $506.03, followed by Colorado at $334.83.** These figures include provisionally undated receipts wherever the purchase location is known. Utah also includes the reported $50 steakhouse payment; the $25 miscellaneous estimate remains in the unknown-state group.

The receipts document purchases in Wyoming, Missouri, Illinois and Kentucky as well as the states described in the itinerary. Tennessee has no included, dated trip purchase in the supplied batch. Missing Tennessee spending should not be read as evidence that nothing was spent there.

## Maverik and Smith's lead the merchant totals

**Maverik totals $225.16, followed by Smith's at $178.53.** The ranked chart shows the eight largest merchants; the table retains every included merchant, so smaller stops are not lost.

Costco totals **$137.53**, versus **$83.28 at Walmart**. Every included Costco dollar is fuel, so this is not a comparison of grocery prices. The two July purchases are excluded from these comparisons; their individual details are withheld. Merchant aliases verified as the same business are grouped; fuel and food at the same stop remain separate transactions.
Use the fuel column to distinguish a high merchant total driven by gasoline from one driven by food or other purchases. All merchant totals below use the same included scope.

## Fully quantified fuel averaged $4.675 per gallon, weighted by gallons purchased

**Fuel spending totals $890.23 across 17 payments with a fuel component.** Of this, $840.23 across 16 fully quantified purchases bought 179.718 gallons. The other $50.00 is your confirmed fuel allocation with unknown gallons, grade, and unit price. Dividing only the quantified fuel charges by their gallons gives **$4.675/gal**. The simple average of printed pump prices is **$4.692/gal**, giving a small fill-up the same weight as a large one. The gallon-weighted average of the printed prices is $4.675/gal; tiny differences from the charged-price calculation reflect receipt rounding.

**The lowest printed price is $4.099/gal at Tumbleweed Express in Laramie, WY, on Aug 17, 2026.** The highest is $5.199/gal at Seibert Travel Stop in Seibert, CO, on Aug 29, 2026. The spread is $1.100/gal; it is an observed trip range, not proof of a persistent state or station price advantage.

The receipts identify **15 premium purchases and one BP Ultimate purchase**; the BP receipt does not print an octane number. These prices should not be compared to regular-grade averages. The table includes the confirmed $50.00 fuel allocation with unknown details clearly labeled and preserves each printed grade, including E10 and 93E10 descriptions, with three-decimal posted prices and volumes. July purchases are excluded. Without distance or odometer readings, the receipts do not support MPG, fuel cost per mile, or total miles driven.

## Aug 17 is the highest-spending dated day

**The highest fully dated daily total is $296.14, from 7 purchases on Aug 17, 2026.** The chart shows every day of the trip, using the local date printed on each receipt. This helps distinguish travel-day purchase clusters from days with fewer supplied receipts; it does not measure time spent in each state.

The bars sum to $1,351.66, not the full $1,501.89 report total. Another **$150.23 has no complete assigned date**: $75.23 of receipt spending plus $75.00 of manual additions. A zero bar means no supplied dated receipt for that day, not verified zero spending. Undated purchases could change the highest-day result.

## Dates and missing expenses are the next useful checks

**The most useful follow-up is to date the $150.23 currently outside the daily chart and confirm whether either July purchase was trip preparation.** The six undated payments remain in aggregate spending but are not individually listed in this public report. Missing dates are left unknown rather than guessed.

Restaurant tips, lodging, online bookings, mileage and any other purchases absent from the supplied material are not recoverable from these receipts. No separately printed tip has been added, and missing tip/tax fields do not prove that a charge was absent. Mixed-category tax splits are approximate. Where an item amount is unreadable, a readable receipt subtotal can support category allocation without inventing a per-item price.

To refine the analysis, add any missing lodging or other payments, give dates for the manual additions if known, and confirm the undated receipts. The frozen v1 totals remain intact; this v2 report applies the documented user-confirmed override and fuel allocation, with its missing fuel quantity and price left visible.

## The companion maps locate purchases, not a reconstructed driving route

**All 43 included image-backed purchases have a map location.** Underlying location matching used 36 address interpolations, 2 verified business locations and 5 city approximations. For privacy, every public map point is rounded to two decimal places and labeled approximate. The public map does not expose exact purchase coordinates or distinguish the original matching precision. These are not GPS observations; merchant and city may still identify a store.

The two manual additions have no point location. Utah is known for the steakhouse, but the exact restaurant is not. Purchase dots can show where money was spent; they do not establish the roads driven, route length, or an exact sequence when dates or times are uncertain.

query.description: Public snapshot of reviewed trip-spending analysis, not a live connection. Original receipts, individual item and payment lookup records, personal identifiers, exact purchase times, street addresses, and private audit evidence are withheld. Selected included fuel-purchase dates, public merchant/city names, grades, quantities and prices remain for comparison. The executable query re-selects this already-sanitized public snapshot for report packaging; it is not the private derivation of the measures. The private calculation queries and original evidence are withheld.
filters: Included trip window: August 14–30, 2026, with undated and manual additions retained in aggregate spending.
Daily spending excludes payments without a complete date; July exclusions are shown only as an aggregate scope group.
metric_definitions: Money is USD. Charged purchase totals are counted once; category amounts include allocated tax and tip where supported.

Fuel quantities and posted unit prices retain three-decimal precision. Weighted effective fuel price uses only charges and gallons from fully quantified purchases. A fuel amount without supplied volume or unit price counts toward spending, not price averages.
query.sql: SELECT snapshot.datasets AS datasets FROM read_json_auto('report-data.json')
